title: A protocol for visualizing active cathepsin K in osteoclasts with a quenched-fluorescence-activity-based probe
protocol: Isolate PBMCs according to the above protocol.
If the PBMC concentration is higher than 1 × 10^6 cells/mL, dilute the PBMCs using supplemented RPMI-1640 medium (with 10% autologous plasma and 50 μg/mL gentamycin).
If the PBMC concentration is lower than 1 × 10^6 cells/mL, centrifuge the tube for 5 min at 300 × g with acceleration and break off set to 8 and 5, respectively.
Discard the supernatant and add supplemented RPMI-1640 medium (with 10% autologous plasma and 50 μg/mL gentamycin) to obtain a final PBMC concentration of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add 1 mL of 1 × 10^6 cells/mL per well of the Nunc™ Lab-Tek™ Chambered Cover glass (Thermo Fisher, 155383).
Mix gently in a figure-eight motion to evenly distribute the cells.
Observe the cells under a light microscope and make sure that cells are distributed evenly.
Place the chamber with cells into an incubator and incubate at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 h.
Prepare α-MEM differentiation medium with 10% FBS and 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin.
Warm the prepared α-MEM differentiation medium to 37°C in a water bath.
Transfer 5 mL of warmed differentiation medium to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Warm the tube containing the differentiation medium in the water bath until it reaches 37°C.
Add 5 μL of fresh RANKL solution (100 μg/mL) and 1.25 μL of fresh MCSF solution (100 μg/mL) to obtain final concentrations of 100 ng/mL RANKL and 25 ng/mL MCSF in the tube.
Incubate cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours with supplemented RPMI-1640 medium containing 10% autologous plasma and 50 μg/mL gentamycin.
Carefully discard the supernatant using a 1 mL pipette.
Wash the wells carefully with dPBS without calcium and magnesium ions.
Add 1 mL of fresh α-MEM differentiation medium containing RANKL and MCSF to every well.
Observe the cells under a light microscope; ensure confluency does not exceed 60% of the well.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2.
Observe the cells under a light microscope every 24 hours for signs of monocyte differentiation.
Exchange the medium every 3-4 days, adding fresh MCSF and RANKL to the media before each exchange.
On Day 13, perform TRAP staining according to the protocol provided.
Terminate differentiation once osteoclasts are observed.
Prewarm 20 mL of deionized water at 37°C.
Prepare two 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes, add 0.5 mL fast garnet GBC base solution and 0.5 mL sodium nitrite solution.
Mix by inversion for 30 s and let stand for 2 min.
Prepare fixative solution by combining 2.5 mL citrate solution, 6.5 mL acetone, and 0.8 mL 37% formaldehyde.
Label a 50 mL centrifuge tube A and add the appropriate ingredients as described in the "Acid phosphate leukocyte kit" section.
Warm centrifuge tube A up to 37°C and check that the temperature is correct before use.
Allow the fixative solution to reach room temperature.
Add 1 mL of fixative solution to 1 well, let stand for 30 seconds, then discard the supernatant.
Rinse the well with deionized water without allowing the slide to dry.
Add 1 mL of solution from centrifuge tube A to the well and incubate for 1 hour at 37°C while protecting the slide from light.
Rinse the slides with deionized water after 1 hour.
Counterstain the slides with 1 mL of hematoxylin solution, Gill no. 3, for 2 minutes.
Remove the supernatant and rinse the wells several times with 1 mL of tap water to remove excess counterstain.
Allow the wells to dry and evaluate under a microscope.
Proceed with confocal slide preparation once osteoclasts can be seen after approximately 14 days of culture.
Treat osteoclasts with inducers or inhibitors based on experimental aims.
Incubate differentiated osteoclasts with selected inhibitors overnight.
Prepare fresh α-MEM differentiation medium with 10% FBS and 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin.
Add TJK16i, E64d, and CA-074Me at a final concentration of 10 μM to separate portions of the medium.
Mix the medium thoroughly before adding it to the cells.
Add 1 mL of inhibitor-containing medium to the osteoclasts.
For control samples, add 1 mL of differentiation medium without inhibitors.
Incubate the cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 24 hours.
Prepare a qTJK16 solution in α-MEM differentiation medium.
Add 5 μL of qTJK16 (initial concentration: 100 μM) to 995 μL of α-MEM differentiation medium with 10% FBS and 100 U/mL penicillin-streptomycin.
Remove the chamber from the incubator, discard the supernatant, and wash the chamber wells.
Add the qTJK16 solution to the appropriate wells.
Incubate cells at 37°C and 5% CO2 for 1 h.
Discard the supernatant by pouring slowly.
Wash the cells with dPBS without calcium and magnesium ions.
Add 1 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde solution to each well and incubate cells for 10 min at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant as described above.
Block the stained cells using blocking buffer for 1 h at room temperature.
Wash the cells with 3 × 1 mL portions of dPBS slowly.
Prepare the antibody solution by adding primary anti-CatK antibody at a ratio of 1:1000 in antibody buffer and mix gently.
Store the working solutions on ice for further experimentation.
Discard the supernatant from each well.
Add 1 mL of antibody solution per well.
Incubate the cells overnight at 4°C.
Select a secondary antibody conjugated with fluorophore for the experiment.
Dilute the selected secondary antibody to a concentration of 1:1000 in antibody buffer.
Discard the supernatant from each well.
Wash the wells with dPBS.
Add 1 mL of diluted secondary antibody solution per well.
Incubate the cells at room temperature for 1 hour.
Prepare an adequate volume of Hoechst 33342 (diluted to a concentration of 1:1000 in dPBS) according to the manufacturer’s instructions and store it no longer than 10 minutes at room temperature.
Discard the secondary antibody from each well after 1 hour incubation.
Wash the cells 3–4 times with dPBS (without calcium or magnesium ions).
Add 1 mL of Hoechst solution per well.
Incubate cells with nuclei staining solution for 10 minutes at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant and wash the wells 2 times with dPBS (without calcium or magnesium ions).
Dissemble the device from the slide by removing the plate cover.
Carefully remove the plastic walls attached to the silicone rubber on the bottom of the slide.
Using tweezers, grab the silicone rubber at a corner and pull slowly to reveal four rectangles.
Use a Kim wipe gently to remove excess supernatant around the tissue pieces.
Add 3 drops of Fluoromount™ Aqueous Mounting Medium to each rectangle on the slide.
Gently place one rectangular coverslip over all wells starting from one end to avoid air bubbles.
Cover the entire surface with mounting medium to avoid dry spots.
Do not squeeze the coverslip against the slide.
Allow the slides to dry in the dark for 30–60 minutes.
Seal the edges of the cover glass using clear nail polish.
Leave the sealed slides to dry for 1 hour, protected from sunlight.
Store the dried slides at 4°C until visualization.
Visualize active CatK in osteoclasts and nuclei with a confocal microscope using lasers set at 405 nm (nucleus), 488 nm (antibody), and 632 nm (qTJK16).
Image samples under a Leica DMi8 confocal microscope equipped with an HC PL APO CS2 63×/1.40 OIL objective.
Set up Z-stack analysis with a step of 0.5–1 microns.
Adjust the laser power for 405 nm to 0.01%, for 488 nm to 3.1%, and for 638 nm to 0.1%.
Determine individual settings based on equipment and expected outcome.
Reduce overexposure of fluorescence signals by adjusting laser power and gain initially on slides with the highest anticipated fluorescence.
Analyze the control slide without staining to ensure that the observed fluorescent signal is not autofluorescence.
Continue analysis of all slides using the same parameters.
Make z-stacks to observe the exact localization of the enzyme and facilitate 3D image generation.
Quantify colocalization by analyzing the morphological features of cells and data quantification from confocal microscopy images.
Calculate Pearson’s correlation coefficient to quantify the proportion between the active enzyme and its total amount in the region of interest.
Compare the intensity of fluorescence to determine differences in CatK activity under different experimental conditions.
Calculate the Pearson’s correlation coefficient for the qTJK16 probe and anti-CatK.
Open images with an available program for image analysis (i.e., LasX®, ImageJ®).
Observe the location of active cathepsin K by visually observing single images.
Use z-stacks to generate a 3D image of an osteoclast.
Analyze at least 10 cells and compare results of imaging from different analyses.
Analyze the fluorescence signal intensity of every captured cell.
Ensure analysis of the z-stack through an entire cell, not just a part of the cell.
Calculate the average of the highest mean intensity per cell of at least 10 cells.
Compare the results in a diagram with the results from other analyses.
